    =
    \begin{pmatrix}
1 \\
\vdots \\
1 \\
2
\end{pmatrix} .
\end{align}
<!-- end mylem-18 -->
<!-- mythm-12: body_md -->
{Components of $\vec{\xi}$ for Type-C Lie Algebras $(n\geqslant2)$}{Components_xi_C}
For the type-C Lie algebra $C_n$ with $n\geqslant2$, the components of the vector $\vec{\xi}$ (see Eq.~\eqref{eq:xi}) are
\begin{align}
     \xi_i
    =
    \begin{cases}
   \dfrac{i(2n+1-i)}{2}\,, &\quad 1\leqslant i\leqslant n-1,
    \\[2ex]
    \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}, &\quad i=n \,.
    \end{cases}
\end{align}
<!-- end mythm-12 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
For $1\leqslant i\leqslant n-1$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:Cn_inverse}, together with the root length vector $\vec{\alpha}$ in Eq.~\eqref{eq:Cn_Root_Length_Vector}, gives
\begin{align}
    \xi_i
    &=
    \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}
    C^{-1}_{ij}
    \langle\alpha_j,\alpha_j\rangle
    +
    C^{-1}_{i n}
    \langle\alpha_n,\alpha_n\rangle\\
    &=
    \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}
    \min\{i,j\}
    +
    \frac{i}{2}\cdot 2
    \\
    &=
    \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}
    \min\{i,j\}
    +
    i.
\end{align}
Evaluating the remaining sum by separating the contributions with $j\leqslant i$ from those with $j>i$ yields
\begin{align}
    \xi_i
    &=
    \left(
   \underbrace{  \sum_{j=1}^{i} j}_{j\leqslant i}
    +
   \underbrace{  \sum_{j=i+1}^{n-1} i}_{j>i}
    \right)
    +
    i
    \\
    &=
    \frac{i(i+1)}{2}
    +
    i(n-1-i)
    +
    i
    \\
    &=
    \frac{i(2n+1-i)}{2}.
\end{align}
For the final node, corresponding to the long simple root $\alpha_n$, we use the last row of $C^{-1}$:
\begin{align}
    \xi_n
    &=
    \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}
    C^{-1}_{n j}
    \langle\alpha_j,\alpha_j\rangle
    +
    C^{-1}_{n n}
    \langle\alpha_n,\alpha_n\rangle
    \\
    &=
    \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}
    j
    +
    \frac n2\cdot 2
    \\
    &=
    \frac{n(n-1)}{2}
    +
    n
    \\
    &=
    \frac{n(n+1)}{2}.
\end{align}
This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- mycor-22: body_md -->
{Type-C Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations $(n\geqslant2)$}{Type_C_Lie_UR}
For the type-C Lie algebra $C_n$ (see Tab.~\ref{tab:Simple_Lie_Algebra}) with $n\geqslant2$, the optimal Lie algebraic uncertainty relation (see Def.~\ref{def:Lie_Algebraic_Uncertainty_Relations}) takes the explicit form
\begin{align}
   \Delta^2_{\psi}( \raisebox{-1.4ex}{\includegraphics[scale=0.8]{DK_C_n.pdf}} )
   \coloneqq
   \Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{sp}(2n,\mathbb C))
   =
    \Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{sp}(n))
    \geqslant
    \left(\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{i(2n+1-i)}{2}\lambda_i\right)+
    \frac{n(n+1)}{2}\lambda_n\,.
\end{align}
The bound is state-independent and is fixed entirely by the representation, through the highest weight $\Lambda$; see Subsec.~\ref{subsec:Highest_Weight_Representations}.
Equivalently, it is determined by the Dynkin coefficient vector $\vec{\lambda}$; 
see Eq.~\eqref{eq:Dynkin_Vector}, together with the type-C root system geometry encoded in $\vec{\xi}$; 
see Eq.~\eqref{eq:xi}.
Its optimality follows directly from Cor.~\ref{cor:Simplified_Lie_Algebraic_Uncertainty_Relations}.
<!-- end mycor-22 -->
<!-- mylem-19: body_md -->
{Entries of $C^{-1}$ for Type-D Lie Algebras ($n\geqslant4$)}{Entries_Cinverse_Type_D}
For the type-D Lie algebra $D_n$, the $(i,j)$-entry of the inverse Cartan matrix is
\begin{align}
\label{eq:Dn_inverse}
    C^{-1}_{ij}
    =
    \begin{cases}
    \min\{i,j\},
    &
    1\leqslant i,j\leqslant n-2,
    \\[1.5ex]
    \dfrac{i}{2},
    &
    1\leqslant i\leqslant n-2,
  \quad\text{and}\quad
    j\in\{n-1,n\},
    \\[1.5ex]
    \dfrac{j}{2},
    &
    i\in\{n-1,n\},
   \quad\text{and}\quad
    1\leqslant j\leqslant n-2,
    \\[1.5ex]
    \dfrac{n}{4},
    &
    i=j\in\{n-1,n\},
    \\[1.5ex]
    \dfrac{n-2}{4},
    &
     i,j\in\{n-1,n\} \quad\text{and}\quad i\ne j.
     \end{cases}
\end{align}
<!-- end mylem-19 -->
<!-- mylem-20: body_md -->
{Root Length Vector $\vec{\alpha}$ for Type-D Lie Algebras ($n\geqslant4$)}{Root_Length_Vector_D}
For the type-D Lie algebra $D_n$ with $n\geqslant4$, the root system is simply laced, so all simple roots have the same squared length.
With the standard normalization in which long roots have squared length $2$, i.e., $\langle\alpha_i,\alpha_i\rangle=2$, the squared simple root lengths form the vector 
\begin{align}
\label{eq:Root_Length_Vector_D}
    \vec{\alpha}
    =\begin{pmatrix}
        2\\
        \vdots\\
        2
    \end{pmatrix}\,.
\end{align}
<!-- end mylem-20 -->
<!-- mythm-13: body_md -->
{Components of $\vec{\xi}$ for Type-D Lie Algebras ($n\geqslant4$)}{Components_xi_D}
For the type-D Lie algebra $D_n$ with $n\geqslant4$, the components of the vector $\vec{\xi}$ (see Eq.~\eqref{eq:xi}) are
\begin{align}
\label{eq:xi_D}
    \xi_i
    =
   \begin{cases}
   i(2n-i-1),
    &\quad
    1\leqslant i\leqslant n-2, \\[2ex]
    \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2} &\quad i\in\{n-1, n\}.
    \end{cases}
\end{align}
<!-- end mythm-13 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
For the nodes along the linear chain (see Eq.~\eqref{eq:Dynkin_D}), $1\leqslant i\leqslant n-2$, the entrywise form of $C^{-1}$ (see Lem.~\ref{lem:Entries_Cinverse_Type_D}) yields
\begin{align}
    \xi_i
    &=
    2\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n-2}\min\{i,j\}
    +
    \frac{i}{2}
    +
    \frac{i}{2}\right)\\
    &=
    2\left(  \underbrace{\sum_{j=1}^{i}j}_{j\leqslant i}
    +
    \underbrace{\sum_{j=i+1}^{n-2}i}_{i<j\leqslant n-2}
    +
    \underbrace{\frac{i}{2}}_{j=n-1}+\underbrace{\frac{i}{2}}_{j=n}\right)\\
    &=
    2\left(\frac{i(i+1)}{2}
    +
    i(n-2-i)
    +
    i\right)\\
    &=
    i(2n-i-1).
\end{align}

For the first terminal node, i.e., $i=n-1$, the corresponding component $\xi_{n-1}$ is obtained from 
\begin{align}
    \xi_{n-1}
    &=
    2\left(\underbrace{\sum_{j=1}^{n-2}\frac{j}{2}}_{j\leqslant n-2}
    +
    \underbrace{\frac n4}_{j=n-1}
    +
   \underbrace{ \frac{n-2}{4}}_{j=n}\right)\\
    &=
    \left(\sum_{j=1}^{n-2}j\right)
    +
    \frac n2
    +
    \frac{n-2}{2}\\
    &=
    \frac{(n-2)(n-1)}{2}
    +
    n-1\\
    &=
    \frac{n(n-1)}{2}.
\end{align}
By the symmetry between the two terminal nodes (see Eq.~\eqref{eq:Dynkin_D}), namely $\alpha_{n-1}$ and $\alpha_n$, one also obtains
\begin{align}
    \xi_n
    =
    \xi_{n-1}
    =
    \frac{n(n-1)}{2}.
\end{align}
This establishes the claimed expression.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- mycor-23: body_md -->
{Type-D Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations ($n\geqslant4$)}{Type_D_Lie_UR}
For the type-D Lie algebra $D_n$ (see Tab.~\ref{tab:Simple_Lie_Algebra}) with $n\geqslant4$, the optimal Lie algebraic uncertainty relation (see Def.~\ref{def:Lie_Algebraic_Uncertainty_Relations}) takes the explicit form
\begin{align}
   \Delta^2_{\psi}( \raisebox{-5.2ex}{\includegraphics[scale=0.8]{DK_D_n.pdf}} )
   &\coloneqq
   \Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{so}(2n,\mathbb C))
   =
    \Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{so}(2n))\\
   & \geqslant
    \left(\sum_{i=1}^{n-2}i(2n-i-1)\lambda_i\right)+\frac{n(n-1)}{2}(\lambda_{n-1}+\lambda_n)\,.
\end{align}
The bound is state independent and is fixed entirely by the representation, through the highest weight $\Lambda$ (see Subsec.~\ref{subsec:Highest_Weight_Representations}).
Equivalently, it is determined by the Dynkin coefficient vector $\vec{\lambda}$ (see Eq.~\eqref{eq:Dynkin_Vector}).
Its optimality follows directly from Cor.~\ref{cor:Simplified_Lie_Algebraic_Uncertainty_Relations}.
<!-- end mycor-23 -->
<!-- mythm-14: body_md -->
{Classical Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations for Adjoint Representations}{Classical_ad}
For rank $n\geqslant 4$, the optimal uncertainty bounds in the adjoint representation reveal a unified structure across the classical Lie algebra families, from type A through type D, as captured by the following correspondences.
\begin{align}
\underbrace{\min_{\psi}2\Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{su}(n+1))}_{\text{Type $\mathrm{A}_n$}}=
\underbrace{\min_{\psi}\Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{so}(2n+1))}_{\text{Type $\mathrm{B}_n$}}+4=
\underbrace{\min_{\psi}2\Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{sp}(n))}_{\text{Type $\mathrm{C}_n$}}=
\underbrace{\min_{\psi}\Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{so}(2n))}_{\text{Type $\mathrm{D}_n$}}+6=
4n.
\end{align}
<!-- end mythm-14 -->
<!-- mythm-15: body_md -->
{Classical Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations for Defining Representations}{Classical_def}
For rank $n\geqslant 4$, the optimal Lie algebraic uncertainty bounds in the defining representation display a unified structure across the classical families of Lie algebras. 
This structure is captured by the following correspondences.
\begin{align}
\underbrace{\min_{\psi}2\Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{su}(n+1))}_{\text{Type $\mathrm{A}_n$}}=
\underbrace{\min_{\psi}\Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{so}(2n+1))}_{\text{Type $\mathrm{B}_n$}}+1=
\underbrace{\min_{\psi}2\Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{sp}(n))}_{\text{Type $\mathrm{C}_n$}}=
\underbrace{\min_{\psi}\Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{so}(2n))}_{\text{Type $\mathrm{D}_n$}}+2=
2n.
\end{align}
<!-- end mythm-15 -->
<!-- mycor-24: body_md -->
{Type-$\mathrm{G}_2$ Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations}{Type_G_Lie_UR}
For the exceptional Lie algebra $G_2$ (see Tab.~\ref{tab:Simple_Lie_Algebra}), the optimal Lie algebraic uncertainty relation (see Def.~\ref{def:Lie_Algebraic_Uncertainty_Relations}) takes the explicit form
\begin{align}
   \Delta^2_{\psi}( \raisebox{-1.4ex}{\includegraphics[scale=1]{DK_G_2.pdf}} )
   \coloneqq
   \Delta^2_{\psi}(\mathfrak{g}_2)
   \geqslant
   6\lambda_1+\frac{10}{3}\lambda_2\,.
\end{align}
The bound is state-independent and is fixed solely by the representation, encoded by the Dynkin coefficient vector $\vec{\lambda}$ (see Eq.~\eqref{eq:Dynkin_Vector}).
<!-- end mycor-24 -->
<!-- mycor-25: body_md -->
{Type-$\mathrm{F}_4$ Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations}{Type_F_Lie_UR}
For the exceptional Lie algebra $F_4$ (see Tab.~\ref{tab:Simple_Lie_Algebra}), the optimal Lie algebraic uncertainty relation (see Def.~\ref{def:Lie_Algebraic_Uncertainty_Relations}) takes the explicit form

   \Delta^2_{\psi}( \raisebox{-1.2ex}{\includegraphics[scale=0.75]{DK_F_4.pdf}})

The bound is state-independent and is fixed solely by the representation, encoded by the Dynkin coefficient vector $\vec{\lambda}$ (see Eq.~\eqref{eq:Dynkin_Vector}).

{Exceptional Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations for Adjoint Representations}{Exceptional_ad}
For the adjoint representations of exceptional Lie algebras, the optimal state-independent uncertainty bounds are given explicitly below.

\underbrace{\Delta^2_{\mathrm{ad}}(\mathfrak{g}_2)}_{\text{Type $\mathrm{G}_2$}}

\underbrace{\Delta^2_{\mathrm{min}}(\mathfrak{f}_4)}_{\text{Type $\mathrm{F}_4$}}

<!-- end mythm-17 -->
<!-- mydef-32: body_md -->
{Simple Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations}{Simple_Lie_UR}
For a quantum state $\rho$ on $V_k(\Lambda_k)$, we define the quantum uncertainty associated with the semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}_k$ by (see Def.~\ref{def:Lie_Algebraic_Uncertainty_Relations})
\begin{align}\label{eq:simple_factor_uncertainty_contribution}
\Delta_\rho^2(\mathfrak g_{k,\mathbb R})
\coloneqq
\frac12
\sum_{a=1}^{\dim\mathfrak g_k}
\Delta_\rho^2\!\left(\widetilde Q_{k,a}\right),
\end{align}
where $\widetilde Q_{k,a}$ is the embedded generator defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:embedded_simple_factor_generator}.
<!-- end mydef-32 -->
<!-- mydef-33: body_md -->
{Semisimple Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations}{Semisimple_Lie_UR}
For a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ with the decomposition in Eq.~\eqref{eq:Semi_Simple}, we define its quantum uncertainty as the sum of the uncertainties associated with its simple components
\begin{align}\label{eq:semisimple_uncertainty_definition}
    \Delta_\rho^2(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb R})
    \coloneqq
    \frac12
    \sum_{k=1}^{s}\sum_{a=1}^{\dim\mathfrak g_k}
    \Delta_\rho^2\!\left(\widetilde Q_{k,a}\right)
    =
    \sum_{k=1}^{s}
    \Delta_\rho^2(\mathfrak g_{k,\mathbb R}),
\end{align}
where each component uncertainty is defined in Def.~\ref{def:Simple_Lie_UR}.
<!-- end mydef-33 -->
<!-- mythm-18: body_md -->
{Semisimple Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations}
{semisimple_LAU_bound}
Let
$\mathfrak g
=
\mathfrak g_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak g_s$
be a complex semisimple Lie algebra, and let
$V(\Lambda)
\cong
V_1(\Lambda_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes V_s(\Lambda_s)$
be an irreducible representation of $\mathfrak g$, with highest weight
$\Lambda
=
\Lambda_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\Lambda_s$.
Suppose that, for each $k=1,\ldots,s$, every quantum state $\sigma_k$ on
$V_k(\Lambda_k)$ satisfies the simple-factor uncertainty bound
\begin{align}\label{eq:simple_factor_assumed_uncertainty_bound}
\Delta_{\sigma_k}^2(\mathfrak g_{k,\mathbb R})
\geqslant
\mathcal{B}_k(\Lambda_k).
\end{align}
Then every quantum state $\rho$ on $V(\Lambda)$ satisfies
\begin{align}\label{eq:semisimple_LAU_bound_componentwise}
\Delta_\rho^2(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb R})
\geqslant
\sum_{k=1}^{s}
\mathcal{B}_k(\Lambda_k).
\end{align}

In particular, applying the simple Lie algebraic uncertainty bound $\mathcal{B}_k(\Lambda_k)=2\langle\Lambda_k,\delta_k\rangle_k$ (see Thm.~\ref{thm:Lie_Algebraic_Uncertainty_Relations}),
where $\delta_k$ is the Weyl vector of $\mathfrak g_k$, gives $\Delta_\rho^2(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb R})\geqslant2\sum_{k=1}^{s}\langle\Lambda_k,\delta_k\rangle_k=2\langle\Lambda,\delta\rangle$, where $\delta=\delta_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\delta_s$.
<!-- end mythm-18 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
For each $k$, let 
$\rho_k
\coloneqq
\Tr_{\widehat{k}} \left(\rho\right)$
be the reduced state on $V_k(\Lambda_k)$. 
Since $\widetilde Q_{k,a}$ acts nontrivially only on the $k$-th tensor factor,
\begin{align}
\Delta_\rho^2\!\left(\widetilde Q_{k,a}\right)
=
\Delta_{\rho_k}^2(Q_{k,a}).
\end{align}
Consequently,
\begin{align}
\Delta_\rho^2(\mathfrak g_{k,\mathbb R})
=
\Delta_{\rho_k}^2(\mathfrak g_{k,\mathbb R})
\geqslant
\mathcal{B}_k(\Lambda_k).
\end{align}
Summing over $k$ 
proves 
Eq.~\eqref{eq:semisimple_LAU_bound_componentwise}.
Variance concavity extends 
$\mathcal{B}_k(\Lambda_k)
=
2\langle\Lambda_k,\delta_k\rangle_k$ to mixed marginals. 
The additive weight metric (see Eq.~\eqref{eq:Inner_root}) gives $2\sum_{k=1}^{s}\langle\Lambda_k,\delta_k\rangle_k$, attained by a product of highest weight states.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- mycor-29: body_md -->
{Simplified Semisimple Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Relations}
{semisimple_Dynkin_coordinate_bound}
Let $\mathfrak{g}=\bigoplus_{k=1}^{s}\mathfrak g_k$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with compact real form $\mathfrak{g}_{\mathbb R}$, and let $V(\Lambda)$ be an irreducible module with highest weight $\Lambda=\bigoplus_{k=1}^{s}\Lambda_k$.
For each simple factor $\mathfrak g_k$, let $C^{(k)}$ denote its Cartan matrix, $\vec{\lambda}^{(k)}$ the Dynkin-label vector of $\Lambda_k$, and $\vec{\xi}^{(k)}$ the corresponding coefficient vector determined by $C^{(k)}$, as tabulated in Tab.~\ref{tab:bounds} and~\ref{tab:exceptional_representations}.
Then Cor.~\ref{cor:Simplified_Lie_Algebraic_Uncertainty_Relations} gives $\mathcal{B}_k(\Lambda_k)=(\vec{\lambda}^{(k)})^{\mathbf{T}}\vec{\xi}^{(k)}$, and every state $\rho$ on $V(\Lambda)$ satisfies
\begin{align}\label{eq:semisimple_Dynkin_coordinate_bound}
\Delta_\rho^2(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb R})
\geqslant
\sum_{k=1}^{s}
\bigl(\vec{\lambda}^{(k)}\bigr)^{\mathbf{T}}
\vec{\xi}^{(k)}.
\end{align}
Defining the vectors, $\vec{\lambda}\coloneqq\vec{\lambda}^{(1)}\oplus\cdots\oplus\vec{\lambda}^{(s)}$ and $\vec{\xi}\coloneqq\vec{\xi}^{(1)}\oplus\cdots\oplus\vec{\xi}^{(s)}$, we can equivalently write
\begin{align}\label{eq:semisimple_bound_lambda_xi}
\Delta_\rho^2(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb R})
\geqslant
\vec{\lambda}^{\,\mathbf{T}}\vec{\xi}  .
\end{align}
<!-- end mycor-29 -->
<!-- mydef-34: body_md -->
{Collective Lie Algebraic Operators}{Collective_Operators}
Let $V(\Lambda)^{\otimes N}$ be the $N$-particle Hilbert space, and let $\{H_i,E_\alpha,F_\alpha\}$ (see Def.~\ref{def:Anti_Hermitian_Basis}) denote the anti-Hermitian single-particle generators of $\mathfrak{g}_{\mathbb R}$ acting on $V(\Lambda)$. 
The corresponding collective operators are obtained by summing their local embeddings over all tensor factors:
\begin{align}
    \mathfrak{H}_i
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{k=1}^N H_i^{(k)}, \quad
    \mathfrak E_\alpha
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{k=1}^N E_\alpha^{(k)}, \quad
    \mathfrak F_\alpha
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{k=1}^N F_\alpha^{(k)} ,
\end{align}
with $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and $\alpha\in\Phi^+$. 
Here each sum is an operator on $\mathcal H\coloneqq V(\Lambda)^{\otimes N}$.
<!-- end mydef-34 -->
<!-- mythm-19: body_md -->
{Lie Algebraic Uncertainty Bounds for Separable Many-Body States}{LAU_Sep_Many_Body}
Any fully separable state $\rho\coloneqq\sum_i p_i\rho_i^1\otimes\cdots\otimes\rho^N_i$ on $\mathcal{H}=V(\Lambda)^{\otimes N}$, with each site carrying the fixed representation $V(\Lambda)$ of $\mathfrak{g}$, must satisfy the many-body Lie algebraic uncertainty bound
\begin{align}
\label{eq:many_body_sep}
    \Delta_{\text{Many-Body}}^2(\mathfrak{g})
    \geqslant N\, \langle \vec{\lambda}, \vec{\xi}\rangle.
\end{align}
Here $\vec{\lambda}$ denotes the Dynkin coefficient vector of the highest weight $\Lambda$, as defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:Dynkin_Vector}, while $\vec{\xi}$ is the vector introduced in Eq.~\eqref{eq:xi}. 
Any violation rules out full separability and therefore certifies entanglement.
<!-- end mythm-19 -->
<!-- mydef-35: body_md -->
{Optimized Collective $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ Uncertainty}{optimized_collective_su3_uncertainty}

For a two-qutrit state $\rho$ on $\mathbb C^3\otimes\mathbb C^3$, we define the optimized collective $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ uncertainty as

\begin{align}\label{eq:optimized_collective_uncertainty}
\mathcal U_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{opt}}(\rho)
\coloneqq
\frac12 \min_{O\in \mathrm{O}(8)} \sum_{a=1}^{8} \Delta_\rho^2  \left(\lambda_a\otimes \1
+\1\otimes \sum_{b=1}^{8} O_{ab}\lambda_b \right) .
\end{align}
<!-- end mydef-35 -->
<!-- mylem-21: body_md -->
{Entanglement Criterion from Optimized Collective Uncertainty}{qutrit_entangle_threshold}
Every separable two-qutrit state $\rho_{\mathrm{sep}}$ satisfies
\begin{align}\label{eq:qutrit_separable_threshold}
\mathcal U_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{opt}}(\rho_{\mathrm{sep}})
\geqslant 4,
\end{align}
where $\mathcal U_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{opt}}$ is defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:optimized_collective_uncertainty}.
Violation of this bound detects entanglement.
<!-- end mylem-21 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
For a fixed $O\in \mathrm{O}(8)$, write
\begin{align}
A_a(O)
\coloneqq\lambda_a\otimes \1 + \1\otimes\widetilde{\lambda}_a .
\end{align}
An orthogonal change of frame leaves the sum of local variances unchanged. Hence, for any single-qutrit state $\phi$ 
\begin{align}
\frac12\sum_{a=1}^{8}
\Delta_\phi^2(\widetilde{\lambda}_a)
=
\frac12\sum_{a=1}^{8}
\Delta_\phi^2(\lambda_a)
=\Delta^2_{\mathrm{def}}( \raisebox{-0.8ex}{\includegraphics[scale=0.8]{DK_A_2.pdf}} )
\geqslant2,
\end{align}
by Eq.~\eqref{eq:single_qutrit_uncertainty_bound_transition}.
Since local variances add on product states and variance is
concave under mixing, every separable state $\rho_{\mathrm{sep}}$
satisfies, for each fixed $O\in \mathrm{O}(8)$,
\begin{align}
\frac12\sum_{a=1}^{8}
\Delta_{\rho_{\mathrm{sep}}}^2
\left(
\lambda_a\otimes\1
+
\1\otimes\widetilde{\lambda}_a
\right)
=\Delta^2_{\mathrm{def}}( \raisebox{-0.8ex}{\includegraphics[scale=0.8]{DK_A_2.pdf}} )+\Delta^2_{\mathrm{def}}( \raisebox{-0.8ex}{\includegraphics[scale=0.8]{DK_A_2.pdf}} )
\geqslant2+2=4.
\end{align}
Minimizing over $\mathrm{O}(8)$ proves the claim.
